name: ops-install
description: Onboarding, and the proof that a repo is actually covered. `/ops-install` detects the repo's branching, CI and release setup, reports capability coverage against catalog.json (present / inherited / missing, by matching ops-<capability> skill names), scaffolds a stub for every missing capability GENERATED from its catalog entry, then interviews the human to fill that stub's TODOs rather than handing over a wall of them — carrying the do-not-select-me guard in the stub's description and never the disable-model-invocation flag, which blocks the Skill tool outright and would leave the capability uncallable by the very loop meant to command it, plus the reject-unknown-action rule and the per-action idempotency requirement — installs the caller workflow on every repo that emits routed events (both repos in a split topology), validates the routing overlay against the event vocabulary and checks every routed loop resolves to an installed skill, then lists the manual steps. Seven of its ten steps are deterministic scripts, starting with a check that the installer itself is up to date, because a coverage report a model produces by reading directories can be quietly wrong. Writes no central config: a capability is found by its name.
